hypothesis: Remove Phase 6 (pt_buf zeroing per window) and the overlap exit zeroing. Since decrypt overwrites exactly `wsize` bytes before search reads them, zeroing is security theater that wastes ~30% of memory bandwidth. This should significantly improve throughput.
Unroll the ChaCha20 round loops using `unroll(10)` to eliminate loop overhead and enable better instruction scheduling in the decrypt phase, which accounts for ~70% of execution time.

Replace 4-block ILP (256B) with 2-block ILP (128B) to reduce register pressure from 23+ to ~13 vector values, fitting within the 16 XMM register file and eliminating costly spills to memory in the critical decrypt loop (~70% of runtime).

Manually inline all rotl16/rotl12/rotl8/rotl7 function calls in the 4-block ILP decrypt loop to eliminate function call overhead. With 320 rotl calls per 256B chunk (32 per double-round × 10 rounds), even 5 cycles of call/return overhead per invocation adds ~1600 cycles per chunk — matching the observed gap between 0.5 GB/s actual and ~1.4 GB/s theoretical. The Ea compiler at opt-level=3 may not inline these helper functions.
